Laukuva First Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Tauragės apskritis, Lithuania

Not demolished. This is the first of Laukuva's two Jewish cemeteries. Jews began settling in Laukuva in the 18th century; the population reached 418 (55 percent) by 1897, and the interwar period saw large-scale emigration to the US, South Africa, and Palestine. About 300 Jews lived in Laukuva on the eve of the 1941 German invasion; men over 15 were taken to the Heydekrug (Šilutė) labor camp and later sent to Auschwitz in 1943, while women and children were murdered in July and December 1941. Seven women and one child, hidden by Lithuanian peasants, survived.
